title: As Driven staged simulator verification observation

source_game_name.description: The name the telemetry client reported for the game, kept exactly as it arrived. Required when `simulator` is `other`, where it is the only record of which game was driven; optional elsewhere, where the canonical id already names it. It is provenance, never a lookup key: it is not normalised, not matched against, and adding a simulator later renames the observation rather than needing the drive repeated.

dataset_version.description: The exact database release loaded when the observation was captured. Optional for compatibility with drafts written before client 0.19.0.

full_throttle_upshift.description: Whether a clutchless upshift went through at sustained full throttle. The first stage of a two-stage test: a 'no' here followed by an accepted lifted upshift is what establishes that the driver must lift, where the lifted result alone shows only that lifting works.

coast_downshift.description: Whether a clutchless downshift went through on a closed throttle. The first stage of a two-stage test: a 'no' here followed by an accepted blipped downshift is what establishes that the driver must blip.

shift_pattern.description: Gate pattern seen in the cockpit. A dogleg layout puts first gear down-left and changes how the car is driven, so it is recorded when visible rather than inferred from the mechanism.

shape.description: Rim family, based on the physical control the driver holds. Use gt-formula for fixed molded grips around a central control face, round for a conventional generally circular rim, d-shaped for a conventional rim with a flattened section, and unknown when the rim was not seen. gt-style, formula, prototype, yoke, and other are deprecated legacy values.

integrated_display.description: Whether the rim itself carries a readout: a graphical LCD, an LED numeric gear indicator, or a segment display all count. A dash mounted on the car rather than the rim does not, and shift lights alone do not.

shift_lights.description: Whether the rim carries shift or rev lights, recorded independently of integrated_display.

open_top.description: For a conventional round or d-shaped rim, whether an upper section of the rim is removed. Use not-applicable for gt-formula.

telemetry.description: The samples the guided-drive results were decided from, kept so a corrected detector can be run over a drive that was already taken instead of asking for it again. Optional: a draft answered by hand, or written before the plugin recorded them, has none. Channels are stored as the telemetry client published them, before any resting offset is subtracted.

sample_rate_hz.description: Median sample rate across the whole drive; null when too few samples arrived to measure it.

resting_throttle.description: Published throttle with the car stopped and untouched before the first test; null when that moment was not seen. A channel already open at rest is not reporting the pedal alone.

resting_clutch.description: Published clutch at the same moment.

free_drive.description: What the free-driving step counted before the driver ended it. These are shifts the gearbox accepted in ordinary driving; a refusal cannot be seen there, so the counts never establish that a lift, a blip or the clutch is required. Three or more like shifts stand in for the scripted test, and the trace kept for that test is then the most recent of them.

full_throttle_upshifts.description: Clutchless upshifts accepted with the throttle held open.

cut_measured.description: Of those, how many published engine torque with the throttle still held through the change.

with_torque_cut.description: Of the measured ones, how many showed a torque collapse.

lifted_upshifts.description: Clutchless upshifts accepted on a lifted throttle.

coast_downshifts.description: Clutchless downshifts on a closed throttle that took drive.

with_throttle_spike.description: Of those, how many were followed by a throttle spike of 15% or more.

shifts_with_clutch.description: Shifts set aside because clutch input was present.

telemetryTrace.description: One guided test's samples. A scripted test's trace ends at the sample that settled the result; a test settled by free driving keeps the samples around the most recent shift that counted. Only a result accepted into the draft has one; a retried or skipped attempt does not.

outcome.description: Whether the detector accepted the maneuver. A rejected first stage is evidence too: it is what establishes that a lift or a blip was needed.

sample_rate_hz.description: Median sample rate over this attempt; null when too few samples arrived to measure it. Below 20 the absence of a brief cut or blip is recorded as unknown rather than no.

columns.description: What each position in a sample holds. t_ms counts from the first sample of the trace; clutch, throttle and brake are percentages; engine_started is 1 or 0. A channel with no usable value is null.

implementation.description: Which installed copy of a car was driven. A simulator with a mod ecosystem reports a name its author chose, so the name identifies the package no better than the package identifies the real car. This block records the package. It makes no claim about which real car the package depicts: that mapping is a reviewed judgement made elsewhere, and it is the risky one.

content_id.description: The simulator's own folder or content identifier for the car, as it reports it. Stable across reinstalls of the same package.

declared_version.description: The version the package declares, when it declares one. Barely half of an installed Assetto Corsa library does, so this is context and never identity.

fingerprint.description:
Answers one question: is this the exact package that was driven? It cannot answer whether two packages behave the same, because the digest covers everything in its scope rather than the shifting behaviour alone. Two digests differing is not evidence that the controls differ, and two matching is not evidence that they do not - compatibility between revisions is a reviewed claim, never inferred from a hash.

It is also not portable between installations as reliably as it looks. A package whose data is unpacked locally digests differently from the same package left packed, so a digest that fails to match another driver's is not evidence of a different car.

scope.description: What was digested. `data-acd` is the packed data file, which is how most Assetto Corsa cars ship and which excludes skins and models while including the gearbox. `loose-data-directory` is a deterministic digest of an unpacked data directory. `gtr2-car-hdc-gear-files` combines the selected GTR2 `.CAR`, its referenced `.HDC`, and its referenced gearbox file.

then.description: An observation from an unregistered simulator must say which game it came from, or `other` is anonymous and two unrelated games become indistinguishable.
